comparisons.success_condition: New cartridge seated, old cartridge placed, door closed, roller untouched versus repeated non-bottoming stops with no adjustment drift.
comparisons.reason: Both include removal/insertion and safety constraints, but they test materially different mechanisms and feedback. Candidate rubric remains incomplete for response and lock verification.

comparisons.objective: Drive and hand off a curved suture needle versus commission a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Arc-following needle rotation, tissue-respecting insertion, and bimanual handoff versus hex-key use, collar adjustment, relocking, and impact tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Needle passes both slots without tear and transfers hands versus two safe carriage stops with stable adjustment.
comparisons.reason: The candidate does not test curved-path penetration or handoff. Candidate missing numeric response and retention limits do not create plausible duplication.

comparisons.objective: Seat and trim a wire on a 110 block versus tune an axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient a punch-down tool, align wire/contact, and apply a terminating stroke versus engage a recessed setscrew, rotate a collar, relock, and cycle-test.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct conductor seated and loose end trimmed without cutting the run versus two acceptable carriage stops and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Both use oriented tools and bounded force, but the functional operations and success evidence differ. Candidate locking and dynamic limits are only partly declared.

comparisons.objective: Open a carton and transfer six fragile eggs versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual lid restraint and repeated gentle fragile-object transfer versus precision key/collar manipulation and dynamic response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: All eggs unbroken and resting in basket versus two non-bottoming stops with stable locked setting.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual care is generic; no common mechanism or tested outcome exists. Candidate lacks complete quantitative damage and drift criteria.

comparisons.objective: Set and lock a telescoping pole to length versus tune and lock a shock absorber for dynamic response.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual counter-twist, axial extension to a mark, retwist, and load test versus hex-key setscrew work, fine collar rotation, repeated impacts, and relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Pole within 10 mm of mark and shortening under 2 mm at 50 N versus two safe stops within 12 mm stroke and a post-lock witness test.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record: both adjust, relock, and verify retention under load. The candidate nevertheless tests a distinct ability—iterative damping calibration from dynamic carriage response plus separate setscrew retention—rather than length setting by coaxial twist. Candidate drift and witness-torque thresholds must still be declared.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative physical impact tests; pr-1865 turns a cabinet hinge side cam to equalize door reveals, then closes/releases the door.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require tool alignment and controlled rotation, but the candidate adds recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew unlock/relock, collar counterholding, bimanual stabilization, bounded tightening, guarded cycle actuation, and adjustment from dynamic stopping response. pr-1865 uses a slotted screwdriver on one cam, avoids decoy screws, and closes the door to inspect static alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable ≥0.85 J impacts at 0.3–3.30 m/s without exceeding 12 mm stroke, hard-stop contact, overload, excessive rebound, or lock drift. pr-1865 requires closed, even 3–6 mm reveals with ≤1 mm difference, ≤0.6 mm proud, no ≥1.2 mm sag, stillness and release for 1 s. Candidate does not yet declare numeric rebound, overload, or drift tolerances; that is a rubric gap but does not make these unrelated outcomes duplicates.
comparisons.reason: The shared generic primitive—engaging and rotating an adjuster—does not establish overlap. The tested ability is meaningfully different: dynamic damper tuning and retention under repeated impacts versus static cabinet-door geometric alignment. All five available pr-1865 spec versions were read and describe the same objective and scoring family.

comparisons.objective: Open a drink can using its recessed stay-on tab versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine tab-tail pinch and lift against a seal versus recessed hex-key engagement, collar rotation, locking, and repeated impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Panel opened by the raised tab versus two safe carriage stops and retained adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Small recessed manipulation is a shared generic challenge, not the same tested ability. Candidate rubric is incomplete for response quality and lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Roll and place an oversized cabinet shelf onto four pins versus tune a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual large-panel reorientation in tight clearance and four-point placement versus fine tool alignment, rotary adjustment, locking, and dynamic cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Shelf level, square, fully back, supported on four pins, and released versus two safe carriage stops and stable lock.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful overlap beyond bimanual coordination. Candidate missing numeric response and witness-test details do not imply duplication.

comparisons.objective: Pipe a shaped icing border versus commission an axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous pressure–motion coordination with deformable material versus rigid small-tool manipulation, rotary tuning, relocking, and impact observation.
comparisons.success_condition: At least five valid joined ridged shells over 80 mm without contamination versus two repeatable safe stops and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: The tested control regimes and physics are unrelated. Candidate lacks fully specified response, overload, drift, and tightening thresholds.

comparisons.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a compact axis shock absorber, then validates repeated carriage stops; record opens a sealed cocktail shaker with a correctly placed blow and separates the tins.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests small-tool insertion, setscrew torque control, collar micro-rotation, counterholding, and iterative adjustment. The record tests localized impulse delivery while stabilizing a tin, followed by separation and upright placement. Bimanual holding and force control are shared only at a generic level.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two compliant physical cycles within stroke and energy limits, with no bottoming, rebound, overload, or setting drift. The record requires a 0.15–<1.0 m/s blow in a defined seam region, seal release, tin removal, upright placement, hand clearance, and no spill/dent/fall. Candidate lacks numeric drift, rebound, overload, and witness-torque tolerances; the record models the seal with code-triggered latches rather than physical vacuum, but the evaluated outcomes remain meaningfully different.
comparisons.reason: Controlled seam striking to release a latch tests impulse placement and post-release handling, whereas damper commissioning tests tool-mediated adjustment, locking, and repeated dynamic-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Replace a damaged drone propeller by removing and reinstalling a threaded nut; candidate commissions a shock absorber through repeated impact-response adjustment and locking.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require bimanual counterholding and tool/fastener rotation, but the record tests propeller removal, placement, thread engagement and nut tightening; the candidate tests recessed hex-key engagement, fine collar tuning, relocking and response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires nut removal, damaged-part disposal, aligned replacement, thread seating/tightness and arms home. Candidate requires two repeatable ≥0.85 J stops within a 12 mm stroke, without hard-stop impact, overload, excessive rebound or lock drift.
comparisons.reason: Shared counterholding and turning primitives do not make the tested abilities equivalent. The candidate uniquely couples fine adjustment and lock retention to measured dynamic stopping behavior. The record supplies complete numeric scoring; candidate collar-drift tolerance is declared but not numerically fixed.

comparisons.objective: Unmold a tart by centering its loose base on a stand and lowering the surrounding ring; candidate commissions and locks an industrial-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests level bimanual rim handling, centered support placement and symmetric lowering without touching a fragile load. Candidate tests small-tool insertion, counterholding, fine collar rotation, torque-limited locking and repeated control actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires the tart/base centered and level on the stand, ring flat on the table, limited ring tilt, no tart contact/displacement, and arms clear/home. Candidate requires two safe repeatable dynamic stops within energy, velocity, stroke, rebound and lock-retention constraints.
comparisons.reason: The objectives, contact regime and failure modes test meaningfully different abilities; generic bimanual coordination is the only material commonality. Both records provide detailed scoring, though the candidate leaves its final collar-drift tolerance to be declared.

comparisons.objective: Insert and prove retention of a ferruled wire in a named terminal versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Target selection, straight constrained insertion, spring-clamp engagement, release, and tensile proof versus setscrew unlocking, collar rotation, relocking, and cycle-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Ferrule home in X1:4 and moves under 1.5 mm at 50 N versus two acceptable carriage stops with collar drift below a declared tolerance.
comparisons.reason: Both end with a retention proof, but terminal insertion tests connector seating while the candidate tests adjustment calibration and fastener locking. Candidate witness torque and drift limits are not yet specified.

comparisons.objective: Perform prove–test–prove voltage-detector procedure versus commission a mechanical damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Button sequencing, temporal indicator interpretation, probe contact, and conditional safe stopping versus tool engagement, fine rotary tuning, relocking, and guarded mechanical cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Detector proves before and after bar contact, or safely aborts on tester failure, versus two non-bottoming stops and stable adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Both require physical controls and verification, but electrical procedural reasoning is materially different from dynamic damping calibration. Candidate response and lock-verification details remain incomplete.

comparisons.objective: Align and release an occluded passive service slider at a visual index; candidate commissions a shock absorber through mechanical adjustment and repeated impact trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Shared fine positioning, but slider manipulation does not require hex-key engagement, setscrew locking, collar adjustment, or response-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Slider requires sub-0.625 mm static alignment and release; candidate requires two safe ≥0.85 J cycles, ≤12 mm stroke, no hard-stop strike/rebound/overload, and bounded collar drift.
comparisons.reason: Static hidden alignment tests a meaningfully different ability from locked, iterative dynamic-damping commissioning. The slider record has no spec version, but its body supplies clear outcome details.

comparisons.objective: Safely stop a spinning centrifuge, open its lid and transfer a sample tube to a rack; candidate tunes and locks a damper for repeatable carriage stopping.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests button pressing, safe-state waiting, hinged-lid opening, tube extraction and upright rack insertion. Candidate tests recessed hex-key use, bimanual stabilization, fine collar tuning, locking torque and iterative response observation.
comparisons.success_condition: Record forbids opening before rotor stop and requires stopped rotor, lid opening, tube removal and upright rack placement without moving the centrifuge or dropping the tube. Candidate requires two consecutive non-bottoming, non-overloaded, low-rebound stops with retained setting.
comparisons.reason: Both include physical control actuation and machinery safety, but their central manipulation and measured capability differ: safe extraction after stopping versus mechanical tuning and retention verified through impacts. The two record spec versions are substantively identical; candidate drift tolerance remains unspecified numerically.

comparisons.objective: Diagnose and repair a keyed fixture by replacing, pinning, and functionally testing a guide; candidate adjusts an installed damper rather than replacing a faulty guide.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve locking and functional verification, but the fixture task tests guide extraction, keyed insertion, pin latching, part orientation, and seating checks—not fine rotary calibration under impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Fixture success uses ≤1 mm seating and 11–13 mm blocking demonstrations in both orientations; candidate requires two dynamically acceptable cycles and a post-lock drift test.
comparisons.reason: Shared maintenance structure does not erase the different tested abilities: component replacement and poka-yoke verification versus iterative dynamic tuning.

comparisons.objective: Bend a copper tube to 90 degrees by iteratively compensating for hidden springback; candidate iteratively tunes and locks a shock absorber from observed stopping response.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both require action-observation-adjustment under hidden response. The record uses large lever motion and release to make an irreversible bend, potentially stabilizing a free bender; the candidate uses precise hex-key engagement, collar micro-rotation, counterholding and bounded lock torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Record scores the relaxed tube angle within 87–93 degrees, lever return and gripper clearance, with failure beyond 96 degrees or if the bender moves/tips. Candidate scores two repeated impacts within stroke, energy and velocity limits, with no hard-stop strike, overload, excessive rebound or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest conceptual match because both test iterative calibration from observed physical response, but the tested manipulation and outcome are materially different: irreversible material forming versus reversible damping adjustment plus mechanical lock retention across repeated impacts. All three record specs were read; they vary mainly in geometry/detail, while the candidate lacks a numeric rebound and drift threshold.

comparisons.objective: Push selected reject cartons from a moving conveyor without disturbing good cartons; candidate commissions a damper on an isolated axis.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed non-prehensile lateral pushing differs from small-tool insertion, threaded locking, fine collar rotation, and dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires both rejects on the table and good cartons preserved throughout; candidate requires two safe, repeatable damped stops and retained adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Moving-line timing and selective pushing do not duplicate adjustment or force-controlled fastening.

comparisons.objective: Mix solutions by waggling test tubes laterally without vertical shaking; candidate adjusts and validates a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled oscillation of tubes differs from tool alignment, setscrew manipulation, fine rotary calibration, and guarded impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: The record’s exact mixing thresholds are not stated in the indexed title/instruction; nevertheless, its objective is clearly mixing without vertical shaking, not dynamic-axis commissioning.
comparisons.reason: Missing comparator thresholds do not create plausible duplication because the manipulated mechanism and tested outcome are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Send a tote down a roller conveyor to a far station without slamming the end stop; candidate mechanically tunes a damper to control repeated carriage stops.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both concern impact management, but the tote task tests direct launch/braking control of a payload; candidate tests recessed-key use, adjuster rotation, lock torque, and iterative hardware calibration.
comparisons.success_condition: Tote success is safe arrival without an end-stop slam; its indexed summary omits exact thresholds. Candidate additionally requires ≥0.85 J tests, published velocity compliance, ≤12 mm stroke, two repeats, and lock-drift verification.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest objective-level relation, but direct tote handling does not test commissioning or retaining an adjustable damping mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Route a connected cable between posts and latch it into a final clip while preserving an existing fixing; candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests articulated-cable routing, bimanual contact, alignment into spring-loaded clip jaws, seating and release. Candidate tests rigid small-tool insertion, counterholding, controlled collar rotation, force-limited locking and dynamic-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires correct routing, both clips seated, both arms contacting the wire for at least 0.2 s each, release, clearance, low wire speed and a 2 s hold; upstream release or wire separation is fatal. Candidate requires two repeatable safe carriage stops and post-lock setting retention.
comparisons.reason: Cable routing and clip latching test deformable/articulated path control and retention, unlike rigid damper adjustment and impact commissioning. No spec versions are indexed for this record, so full setup geometry and some numeric routing/clip predicates are missing, but the body gives enough objective, manipulation and scoring evidence to establish a meaningful distinction.

comparisons.objective: Install a booster-seat tray and latch both sides at the second notch; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual alignment and snap-latching differ from hex-key insertion, setscrew torque, collar calibration, and response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Tray must be seated and locked bilaterally at a specified notch; candidate requires repeated safe dynamic stops and no setting drift.
comparisons.reason: A latch-installation task does not test adjustable damping or guarded commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Compress and lock spring tongs, then place them in a cutlery tray; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Spring compression and latch engagement differ from recessed fastener operation, fine collar adjustment, and iterative impact observation.
comparisons.success_condition: Tongs must remain locked shut in the tray; exact indexed tolerances are absent. Candidate instead requires quantified dynamic and retention outcomes.
comparisons.reason: The shared notion of locking is too generic to establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Operate a real mouse to drag a screen file into a folder; candidate physically adjusts industrial hardware.
comparisons.physical_skill: Mouse grasping, cursor control, button holding, and release differ from bimanual counterholding, tool insertion, torque control, and damper tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires a successful GUI drag-and-drop and mouse release; candidate requires physical cycle performance and retained mechanical adjustment.
comparisons.reason: The task interfaces and tested abilities are plainly different.

comparisons.objective: Depress a case hub, extract a disc, reorient it upright, and insert it into a slot-loading console; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hub release, delicate edge grasping, regrasping, and slot insertion differ from hex-key fastening and iterative rotary calibration.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires disc release and successful console insertion without damage; candidate requires two compliant carriage stops and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Shared insertion primitives are incidental and do not duplicate the candidate’s calibration ability.

comparisons.objective: Bimanually flex a build plate to release a printed part without kinking it; candidate commissions an adjustable damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Distributed elastic bending and part capture differ from recessed tool engagement, controlled collar rotation, tightening, and cycle-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires part release into a bin and plate returned flat; candidate requires quantified impact behavior and post-lock stability.
comparisons.reason: Force control is shared only generically; the tested mechanics and failure modes differ.

comparisons.objective: Seat a platform on cone, V-groove, and flat kinematic datums; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual level lowering and three-point precision seating differ from small-tool use, threaded locking, collar rotation, and iterative response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: All three feet must bear on their matching datums with the platform released; candidate requires two safe cycles and retained adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Precision seating tests geometric constraint alignment, not dynamic damping calibration.

comparisons.objective: Bimanually guide and rotate foam through a fixed hot ribbon along a printed curve; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous coordinated path following and cutting differ from tool insertion, rotary adjustment, tightening, and impact-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires completing the curved cut and clearing the hot ribbon; exact dimensional tolerance is not present in the indexed summary. Candidate uses dynamic stop and retention criteria.
comparisons.reason: Missing cut tolerance does not suggest duplication of a mechanically adjusted damping task.

comparisons.objective: Level a rack shelf by relocating the single pull pin in the wrong hole; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Shelf support, spring-pin retraction, hole alignment, and reinsertion differ from recessed hex-key use, collar calibration, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Shelf must rest level on all four pins; candidate requires two repeatable safe impacts and no collar drift.
comparisons.reason: Both are maintenance adjustments, but the tested latching/alignment ability is materially different from response-based damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Separate two linked S-hooks and hang each on a separate support without putting either down; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual in-hand reorientation, unhooking, and hanging differ from counterholding, hex-key engagement, fine rotation, and tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Hooks must be separated and independently supported without an intermediate set-down; candidate requires quantified dynamic performance and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective or success-condition overlap exists.

comparisons.objective: Hold a nail upright while the other arm hammers it until self-supporting; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization under repeated impacts is shared, but nail holding and hammer striking differ from recessed fastener use, collar adjustment, and calibration.
comparisons.success_condition: Nail must become self-supporting and the holding arm must clear the hammer; candidate must avoid hard-stop impact while achieving two repeatable damped cycles and retained setting.
