comparisons.success_condition: Sensor must remain below 50 g and retained after a 30 cm drop; candidate must stop a carriage twice without bottoming, rebound, overload, or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Both evaluate shock outcomes, but one tests protective packaging assembly and the other tests iterative mechanical damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: The PR renames a category; its included example extends a telescoping lamp. Candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Example uses base stabilization and stem pulling; candidate uses recessed-tool engagement, fine rotation, counterholding, and locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Example scores extension height while limiting base lift and tilt; candidate scores dynamic stops and setting retention.
comparisons.reason: Neither the metadata change nor the complete lamp example duplicates damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Select and hand off the requested M4×20 screw; candidate adjusts a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual size selection, small-part grasping, and tray placement versus hex-key insertion, collar tuning, and bounded locking torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one correct screw must lie near the tray floor; candidate requires safe repeated carriage stops and no drift.
comparisons.reason: Small-part handling is a generic shared challenge, not the same tested mechanical ability.

comparisons.objective: Order and shelve four books by spine code; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Edge pinching, reorientation, ordered insertion, and placement between books versus precision tool use and iterative adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: All books upright, outward-facing, and alphabetically ordered; candidate requires verified impact performance and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: The tasks have unrelated objectives and success predicates.

comparisons.objective: Route a rigid bar beneath a bracket to a stop; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Low-clearance translational insertion and planar alignment versus hex-key engagement, rotational adjustment, counterholding, and cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Bar lies flat between clip posts within 8 mm of the stop; candidate must satisfy dynamic stroke, impact, rebound, overload, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: A constrained insertion task does not test iterative dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Sort glasses and plates into appropriate racks with ordered plate stacking; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated bimanual handoffs, upright placement, and size-ordered stacking versus fine tool alignment and mechanical tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct locations and order with nothing tipped, dropped, or misrouted; candidate requires two safe physical test cycles and retained setting.
comparisons.reason: Only generic bimanual handling is shared.

comparisons.objective: Sort rubbish into bins according to a material rule; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Classification and pick-and-place across bins versus recessed-tool insertion, counterholding, fine rotation, and force control.
comparisons.success_condition: Every item must enter its rule-defined bin; candidate requires bounded dynamic response and a locked, drift-resistant setting.
comparisons.reason: Classification-based sorting does not overlap with mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Join two single-stud blocks and verify the connection by lifting; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stud alignment, press-fit insertion, and retention testing versus setscrew unlocking, collar rotation, locking, and impact cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Connection must carry the lower block during a lift; candidate must produce two non-bottoming stops and retain adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Both include a physical verification step, but one tests press-fit assembly and the other dynamic parameter tuning.

comparisons.objective: Join a 1×1 block to a corner of a 2×2 block and verify retention; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Corner selection, stud alignment, press-fit insertion, and lift testing versus tool-mediated unlocking and adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Upper block must retain the base during lifting; candidate requires repeated safe carriage deceleration and lock stability.
comparisons.reason: Geometry is not the basis for novelty here; the underlying assembly and commissioning skills are different.

comparisons.objective: Open a pump suction valve before starting the pump; candidate adjusts a damper while isolated, then operates a guarded cycle control.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered valve and button operation versus precision hex-key/collar manipulation plus later control actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Safe sequence leaves the pump running with suction open; candidate requires de-energized adjustment and two measured safe stops.
comparisons.reason: Both enforce safe sequencing around energized equipment, but the pump task does not test adjustment, locking, or dynamic-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Measure and place a block 10 cm beyond a reference line; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ruler use, spatial measurement, and placement versus precision tool engagement and iterative mechanical adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Block center must be within 1 cm for full credit and rest on the table; candidate uses stroke, impact, rebound, overload, and drift criteria.
comparisons.reason: Measurement-guided placement and dynamic commissioning are unrelated tested abilities.

comparisons.objective: Remove a file and place an out-card in its exact shelf gap; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Packed-row extraction, gap preservation, bimanual handoff, and thin-card insertion versus hex-key use and collar tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: File and card must occupy their prescribed destinations without disturbing neighbors; candidate requires repeatable safe stops and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Constrained shelf manipulation does not duplicate mechanical response adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Lower a ratchet-supported load through an intermediate hold and restart; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load transfer, crank control, pawl release, regrasping, and contact-supported holding versus setscrew/collar adjustment and test cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Load must hold on an intermediate tooth before final lowering; candidate must stop a carriage twice without bottoming or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Both involve energy-bearing mechanisms and guarded restart, but one tests ratchet load handling while the other tests adjustment of dissipative response.

comparisons.objective: Stack boxes with the heavy case at the bottom; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Mass-aware lifting, placement, and stable stacking versus fine tool manipulation and iterative response correction.
comparisons.success_condition: Heavy case must form the stable base and no box may tip beyond 30 degrees; candidate requires bounded impact behavior and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: The manipulation and success logic are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Solvent-join a PVC pipe to a tee using insertion, a quarter turn, and a timed hold; candidate rotates and locks a damper collar.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual fitting stabilization, axial insertion, quarter-turn assembly, and sustained holding versus hex-key unlocking, fine adjustment, and torque-limited relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Assembly must occur while wet, seat fully, turn, and remain held for 30 seconds; candidate must pass two dynamic cycles and a witness-torque drift test.
comparisons.reason: Rotational manipulation is shared, but the PVC task tests joint assembly and cure retention, not iterative tuning or an adjustable lock.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative dynamic tuning; pr-727 removes a strong magnet from a steel plate and places it at least 5 cm away without reattachment.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key insertion, setscrew loosening/torque-limited relocking, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and repeated physical cycling. pr-727 requires bimanual plate restraint, tangential magnet sliding by a knob, controlled separation, placement, and release. Bimanual stabilization is shared only as a generic primitive.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable ≥0.85 J impacts within the stated velocity range, ≤12 mm travel, no hard-stop strike/overload/excess rebound, and bounded post-lock collar drift, with safety and anti-state-write constraints. pr-727 requires holding the plate, setting the magnet down ≥5 cm away, releasing it, and preventing snap-back. Its indexed record has no spec versions and does not define numeric plate-retention or snap-back thresholds beyond the 5 cm placement distance.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities are meaningfully different: tool-mediated adjustment and retention followed by dynamic damper validation versus force-controlled magnetic separation and safe placement. Different geometry is not the basis of the verdict, and the shared generic bimanual element does not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Inspect hidden labels and dispense only the 10 mg medicine pack; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Reorienting look-alike cartons, visual inspection, selection, and placement versus precision tool use and mechanical adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Only the correct strength may be dispensed; candidate requires safe repeated impact response and retained collar setting.
comparisons.reason: The medicine task tests active perception and selection, not commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Hold an LED flush while touching a soldering-iron tip to a pad, then return the iron safely; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual component restraint, millimeter-scale tool contact, timed holding, and safe tool return versus recessed hex-key alignment, counterholding, and rotational adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: LED must remain flush during two seconds of pad contact and the iron must return tip-first; candidate requires two safe physical cycles and no setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Both demand precise bimanual tool use, but the contact operation, mechanics, and verified outcomes are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Install, quarter-turn, and position a T-nut in an extrusion slot; candidate commissions a shock absorber through iterative impact testing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained insertion, in-slot rotation, and sliding versus hex-key engagement, collar adjustment, locking, and dynamic-response evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: T-nut locked under slot lips and released at a mark versus two safe, repeatable non-bottoming cycles with retained setting. No separate spec version or numeric placement tolerance is provided.
comparisons.reason: The tested mechanism and outcome differ materially; shared fine rotation and positioning are only generic primitives.

comparisons.objective: Make five flat sanding passes along a plywood edge; candidate tunes and locks an axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained flat abrasive contact and reciprocation versus recessed-tool insertion, fine collar rotation, torque-limited locking, and impact-cycle diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Five full passes while flat without workpiece slip versus two dynamically acceptable stops without bottoming, rebound, overload, or drift. No separate spec version is provided.
comparisons.reason: Surface finishing does not test adjustment retention or dynamic energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Dispense three drops, cork a tube, then perform four counted shakes from memory; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Liquid dispensing, cork insertion, shaking, and action counting versus tool alignment, counterholding, collar tuning, and force-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Exact action counts and restored objects versus measured stopping behavior across repeated physical cycles. The record supplies no numeric spill or seating rubric and no separate specs.
comparisons.reason: The principal tested ability is sequential counting with lab manipulation, not mechanical tuning.

comparisons.objective: Recognize a failed autoclave load and place it on hold for reprocessing rather than releasing it; candidate commissions a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Indicator/reference reading, sign placement, and pail handling versus precise mechanical adjustment and dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Pail held on the mat with HOLD marking, avoiding false treated status, versus locked setting producing safe carriage stops. No separate specs or quantitative pail criteria are provided.
comparisons.reason: This is a safety-judgment and material-handling task, not a force-response commissioning task.

comparisons.objective: Verify equipment identity and clearance before sending a laboratory mixer for repair; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Serial-card matching, tag handling, and equipment transport versus hex-key use, collar adjustment, counterholding, and impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Uncleared mixer remains tagged while only appropriate items move to the cart versus two compliant damper cycles. No separate specs or geometric thresholds are provided.
comparisons.reason: Identity-based decontamination safety is meaningfully different from mechanical response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Inspect covered cases and return an instrument module to the empty one; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual lid manipulation, camera inspection, carrying, and case insertion versus recessed setscrew manipulation and iterative dynamic adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Module placed in the unoccupied case; entering an occupied case permanently fails. Candidate instead requires safe repeated stopping and lock retention. No separate specs or insertion tolerances are supplied.
comparisons.reason: Occupied-case selection and module stowage do not test adjustable damping or setting retention.

comparisons.objective: Withdraw an index latch, swing a footrest, and settle it into its stowed capture; candidate commissions and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual latch withdrawal and hinged-part swinging versus hex-key insertion, collar rotation, counterholding, and controlled tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Footrest reaches and remains in capture after the latch-mediated swing versus two safe impact cycles with negligible setting drift. Exact capture bands are referenced but absent; no separate specs exist.
comparisons.reason: Although both contain unlocking and final retention, one tests indexed hinged stowage and the other dynamic parameter tuning.

comparisons.objective: Stabilize a light engine while rapidly pulling its recoil starter through a 30 cm stroke; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual reaction-force bracing and high-speed long-stroke pulling versus precision tool engagement, fine rotation, locking torque, and iterative testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Full 30 cm pull in under 0.5 seconds without dragging the engine versus repeated non-bottoming stops within a 12 mm damper stroke. No separate specs are present.
comparisons.reason: The task tests fast power-stroke execution and stabilization, not adjustment of impact response.

comparisons.objective: Stage and time a gravity release so a ball enters an empty moving tray; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Gate sequencing and motion timing versus fine mechanical adjustment, locking, and diagnosis from repeated impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Ball lands in the empty rather than occupied tray under varied layouts versus two safe stops with retained adjustment. No separate specs or tray tolerances are provided.
comparisons.reason: Predictive timing of a ballistic release is not dynamic damping calibration.

comparisons.objective: Insert a server power cord and close its retention latch; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plug alignment/insertion with bimanual latch closure versus hex-key engagement, counterholding, collar tuning, and torque-bounded relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Powered indication, fully seated plug, and latch holding after release versus acceptable impact behavior and post-lock drift tolerance. No separate specs or insertion-force thresholds are given.
comparisons.reason: Both use retention, but the record tests connector seating and latch closure rather than iterative response adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Relocate a bar while keeping a loose reflector ball balanced on it; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Careful transport with balance preservation versus small-tool manipulation, collar rotation, tightening, and physical cycle evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Bar reaches the pad while the ball never touches table or pad versus safe repeated carriage stops. No separate specs or pose tolerances are provided.
comparisons.reason: Balance-preserving transport tests a different control ability from damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Choose a water bath rather than a microwave and place a baby bottle safely for warming; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Method selection and upright bottle placement versus tool insertion, mechanical tuning, counterholding, and locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Stable upright bottle with neck above water and microwave unused versus two non-bottoming, non-rebounding cycles with retained setting. Heat transfer is explicitly not simulated; no separate specs exist.
comparisons.reason: The record tests safety-method selection and placement, not mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Steady a light printer while pulling its magnetically caught door fully open; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization, catch breakaway, and hinged-door motion versus precision hex-key use, collar adjustment, torque control, and dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Door remains at its open stop without printer displacement or protected-part contact versus repeated acceptable damper stops. No separate specs or exact displacement thresholds are supplied.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual counterforce is generic; the mechanisms and measured outcomes differ.

comparisons.objective: Counterhold a copper riser, operate a tube cutter until separation, and discard the cut piece; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated cutter orbiting with workpiece stabilization and post-cut handling versus recessed setscrew manipulation, collar tuning, and impact assessment.
comparisons.success_condition: Pipe separates at the mark and offcut reaches the scrap bucket versus locked adjustment yielding safe repeatable stopping. No separate specs or cut tolerance is provided.
comparisons.reason: Material cutting and separation are not adjustment or energy-absorption commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Replace failed and predictive-failure drives in a safe rebuild sequence; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Drive extraction/insertion, state monitoring, and ordered waiting versus fine tool alignment, adjustment, locking, and dynamic diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Failed drive replaced first, rebuild completed, then amber drive replaced without array loss versus two compliant impact cycles. Drive seating tolerances are absent and no separate specs exist.
comparisons.reason: The core ability is state-dependent maintenance sequencing, not tuning a mechanical response.

comparisons.objective: Lever a heavy block upward, insert a chock, and transfer load onto it; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual lever-force application and under-load chock placement versus small-tool manipulation and iterative impact-response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Two-kilogram block rests safely on the chock after bar release versus safe stopping across two cycles with setting retention. No separate specs or lift/chock tolerances are given.
comparisons.reason: Load lifting and support transfer test different mechanics from damping calibration.

comparisons.objective: Select and seat corrosion-compatible fittings in two mixed-metal pipe gaps; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Part classification, orientation, and coupling insertion versus hex-key alignment, collar adjustment, counterholding, and controlled tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Correctly oriented dielectric union and copper coupling seated and released without disturbing the run versus validated dynamic stops. Seating tolerances are absent and no separate specs exist.
comparisons.reason: Correct fitting selection and insertion do not test adjustable energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Encode “hid” in correctly oriented Braille cells using balls; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated ball placement plus spatial-symbol reasoning versus precision mechanical tool use and response-based adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: All three letters have correct dot patterns and reader-side orientation versus two safe, repeatable locked damper cycles. No separate specs or cup-placement tolerances are supplied.
comparisons.reason: Symbolic spatial assembly is unrelated to dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Align a robot elbow’s zero marks while inserting and releasing a mastering pin; candidate commissions a robot-axis shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual joint support, visual alignment, and pin insertion versus counterholding, hex-key insertion, collar tuning, torque-limited locking, and cycle testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Marks aligned, pin home, green indication, and joint retained after release versus two non-bottoming stops with no excessive rebound or drift. No separate specs or alignment tolerances are provided.
comparisons.reason: Both concern robot maintenance and alignment, but mastering establishes joint datum through pin insertion; the candidate tunes and verifies dynamic energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Hand off, align, and insert a cable-bound duplex fibre connector; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Inter-arm transfer, cable-constrained retention, and submillimetric dual-peg insertion versus small hex-tool engagement, collar rotation, tightening, and impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Connector remains inserted after release and retreat for 20 seconds versus locked adjustment producing two safe cycles. The record gives clearances but no separate specs.
comparisons.reason: Precision connector insertion under cable load is materially different from dynamic response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Select the dry mould and bimanually lift, carry, and pour a crucible using its shank; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hazard recognition, two-handle load transport, and controlled pouring versus precision adjustment-tool use and iterative impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Rigid beads poured into the dry mould without touching the crucible or choosing the wet mould versus repeatable non-bottoming stops. Pour quantity/tolerance is unspecified and no separate specs exist.
comparisons.reason: Foundry-safe material transfer does not test damping adjustment or lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Seat a vessel upright in a bay while maintaining clearance from a crew hand; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Collision-aware transport and upright placement versus hex-key engagement, fine adjustment, counterholding, and torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: Vessel within 5 degrees upright and at least 5 cm from the hand versus two safe impact cycles with retained setting. No separate specs are supplied.
comparisons.reason: Human-clearance-aware placement is a different tested ability from mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Hold a washed part over its bath to drain before moving it to a rack; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed holding and contamination-aware transport versus tool alignment, collar tuning, locking, and repeated dynamic observation.
comparisons.success_condition: At least three seconds stationary above the bath before transfer versus two dynamically acceptable stops. No separate specs or drain/spill thresholds are provided.
comparisons.reason: The core constraint is dwell-before-transport, not mechanical adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Support a door, align interleaved hinge knuckles, and insert a pin through all five; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual heavy-part alignment and long coaxial pin insertion versus counterholding, recessed hex-key use, fine collar rotation, and tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Door supported by a pin passing through all five knuckles versus safe repeated stopping with locked setting. No numeric hinge clearances or separate specs are provided.
comparisons.reason: Hinge assembly tests simultaneous alignment and insertion, not dynamic tuning.

comparisons.objective: Seat a keyed coupling over unequal drive dogs and prove torque transfer; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed rotational alignment, coupling insertion, release, and rotor actuation versus hex-key engagement, collar tuning, locking, and impact-cycle diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Coupling aligned within 5 degrees, stably seated after release, and transmitting drive versus two non-bottoming stops with bounded rebound and drift. No separate specs exist.
comparisons.reason: Both include rotation and functional verification, but coupling assembly verifies kinematic drive transfer while the candidate adjusts and validates dissipative response.

comparisons.objective: Control closure of a gravity-loaded cover; unlike commissioning a damper through repeated impact trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support transfer and speed-controlled closing, not hex-key unlocking, collar tuning, or relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Constrained closing speed; no numeric limit is given. No spec versions are present.
comparisons.reason: Both regulate motion safely, but they test different mechanisms and manipulation abilities.

comparisons.objective: Chock a rolling cradle before unloading it, rather than tune a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual chock placement followed by load transfer; no fine rotary adjustment or tool engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both chocks seated, cradle controlled, load placed, grippers released. Thresholds are omitted; no spec versions are present.
comparisons.reason: Generic stabilization and safety sequencing do not create meaningful overlap.

comparisons.objective: Move two cord-linked devices onto a shelf without tensioning their cord.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated transport of tethered objects and cord management, not adjuster manipulation or dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Everything rests on the shelf without dragging, hanging, or cord pulling. No numeric tension limit or spec versions are provided.
comparisons.reason: The constrained transport ability is unrelated to commissioning an energy absorber.

comparisons.objective: Mark specified answers on a printed form, not adjust machinery.
comparisons.physical_skill: Marker grasping and precise planar contact; no unlocking, fine mechanical tuning, or impact observation.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct boxes marked and wrong boxes unmarked. Mark-quality thresholds and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: The tested writing and semantic-selection ability is meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Orient and seat a filter cartridge according to its flow arrow.
comparisons.physical_skill: Read part orientation, rotate it, and perform seated insertion; no tool-driven adjustment or response-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Cartridge flat and arrow downstream. Seating tolerances and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Part orientation and insertion differ from iterative damper commissioning despite shared fine manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Safely reset a breaker by switching its load off first, rather than mechanically tune a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered switch and breaker actuation; no collar counterholding, hex-key work, or iterative adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Load off, breaker reset, load restored, motor running. Timing and electrical thresholds and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Both include safe de-energized sequencing, but the central tested abilities are different.

comparisons.objective: Route a fibre cord through a guide without violating bend radius.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable routing and connector placement, not rigid-body tool engagement or damping adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Connector seated, cord against guide, bend radius never below 25 mm. No spec versions are present.
comparisons.reason: This tests continuous cable-shape control rather than mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Interpret a compass card and place a cube on the north pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual-spatial reference interpretation and pick-and-place only.
comparisons.success_condition: Cube center within the correct pad and at most 2 cm above support. No spec versions are present.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, skill, or success-condition overlap exists.

comparisons.objective: Read name cards and place cups at two invited guests' locations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic matching and ordinary pick-and-place, not tool use or dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Cups must occupy Ana's and Sam's places; exact placement tolerances and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: The task tests identity-to-location grounding rather than machine adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Restore monitoring by refitting a displaced finger probe instead of silencing an alarm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-clearance placement over a fingertip; no threaded tool alignment, collar rotation, or iterative commissioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Probe refitted with 3 mm clearance per side and reading restored; silencing alone fails. No spec versions are present.
comparisons.reason: Safety-aware insertion is meaningfully different from response-based damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Orient and insert a DIP chip into a ZIF socket, then close its lever.
comparisons.physical_skill: In-air reorientation, pin-slot insertion, and ordered latching; no tuning from dynamic feedback.
comparisons.success_condition: Notch faces lever, pins enter slots, lever closes afterward. Numeric insertion tolerances and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Although both include a retained mechanism and fine manipulation, chip insertion tests a different ability.

comparisons.objective: Keep a lock key turned while pulling a drawer open.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual sustained rotation and simultaneous pulling, not iterative parameter adjustment or torque-bounded relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Quarter-turn held until drawer motion begins. Angle tolerance, opening distance, and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Shared rotation and bimanual coordination are generic; the sustained interlock operation is different.

comparisons.objective: Unlay a layered hose from the correct exposed end and route it to a hydrant pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long deformable-object extraction and routing, not rigid fine adjustment or tool use.
comparisons.success_condition: Hose end reaches the pad and is released. Bend, snag, and placement thresholds and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: The tested deformable-routing ability is unrelated to damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Drift a structural splice into alignment, insert two bolts, and return the drift.
comparisons.physical_skill: Forceful alignment with a drift followed by bolt insertion, not response-based adjustment of damping.
comparisons.success_condition: Plate aligned, both bolts inserted, drift returned. Alignment and insertion tolerances and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Actual alignment and insertion are meaningfully different from tuning and locking an adjuster.

comparisons.objective: Candidate commissions and mechanically locks a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative impact testing; pr-1101 probes a duct to locate a blockage, marks its position, and withdraws the probe.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew unlocking/locking, collar fine-rotation, counterholding, bounded torque, and response-based tuning. pr-1101 requires advancing a long rod until obstruction contact, mapping that contact to an exterior marker position, marker placement, and rod withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires physical unlock-adjust-relock operations and two repeatable ≥0.85 J cycles within specified velocity/stroke, rebound, overload, hard-stop, and drift limits. pr-1101 only states that the blockage must be found, marked above the duct, the rod removed, and released; it provides no numeric localization tolerance, contact-force/damage limit, withdrawal deadline, or hold duration, and has no spec versions.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities are meaningfully different: closed-loop dynamic damper adjustment and retention under repeated impacts versus contact-based blockage localization and spatial marking with a probe. Generic contact and object manipulation do not establish overlap, and pr-1101’s missing numeric rubric details do not plausibly make its objective equivalent to damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Perform ordered gold lift-off and rinsing while containing contaminated drips.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual liquid-process handling, cassette transfer, and drip-dish coordination.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct beaker and rinse order, cassette left in final rinse, all waste captured. Quantitative contamination limits and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: This tests wet-process sequencing and spill prevention, not mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Flush an emergency eyewash until clear, shut it, and cap its heads.
comparisons.physical_skill: The body gives no manipulation detail beyond valve operation and cap replacement; no fine damper adjustment is established.
comparisons.success_condition: Water clear, flow shut, heads capped. Flow, clarity, duration thresholds and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Despite sparse rubric detail, the clearly stated inspection-and-restoration objective is unrelated to shock-absorber tuning.

comparisons.objective: Unclog a double sink while sealing the coupled drain.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained bimanual sealing plus at least four plunger strokes, followed by tool stowage.
comparisons.success_condition: Other drain held shut, four or more pumps, water drains, tools restored, arms returned. No spec versions are present.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual force coordination is shared only generically; the pumping task tests a different mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Form a straight steel bar into a rectangular stirrup using three marked bends.

comparisons.reason: Although both adjust industrial fixtures, static geometry setup does not test response-guided damping or lock retention under witness torque. Specs and numeric tolerances beyond 16:1 are missing.

comparisons.objective: Seat and split a tablet in a V-cradle, versus commission a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-object seating and controlled blade closure/fracture versus recessed-tool alignment, collar tuning, counterholding, and tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Tablet correctly seated and divided versus two safe repeatable stops with no hard-stop strike or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Controlled cutting/fracture is unrelated to dynamic damper tuning. Body and specs are absent, so split quality and damage thresholds are missing.

comparisons.objective: Cut a wire-duct cover to length and snap it over an open run, versus tune and lock a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Length fitting, cutting, long-part alignment, and distributed latching versus fine tool insertion, rotary adjustment, counterholding, and witness-torque locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Duct run fully covered with a fitted, latched cover versus two quantified safe impacts and retained collar setting.
comparisons.reason: Cover fitting/latching does not test adjustable energy absorption. Body and specs are absent, so fit, cut, and latch tolerances are missing.

comparisons.objective: Draw a self-retracting lifeline below lock speed and hook it to a harness D-ring, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Speed-regulated tether extraction, hook alignment, and latching against retraction versus small-tool engagement, fine adjustment, tightening, and impact-cycle observation.
comparisons.success_condition: Lifeline extended without triggering its lock and hook secured versus two non-bottoming stops and drift-resistant adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Both concern velocity-sensitive equipment, but tether handling/latching does not tune or validate an impact absorber. Body/spec thresholds, including lock speed, are missing.

comparisons.objective: Start and close a separating zipper, versus tune and lock a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Flexible pin/box alignment, insertion, tension management, and slider travel versus rigid hex-key alignment, collar rotation, counterholding, and force-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin fully seated and zipper closed versus two safe repeatable dynamic stops with setting retention.
comparisons.reason: Flexible interlocking-chain manipulation is a different tested ability. Body and specs are absent, so zipper engagement and damage criteria are missing.

comparisons.objective: Refit a foam air-filter element so it seals around its perimeter, versus commission a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compliant-part placement, edge tucking, and distributed seal inspection versus rigid fine-tool manipulation, rotary tuning, tightening, and impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Filter seated with a continuous seal versus two quantified safe carriage stops and no collar drift.
comparisons.reason: Deformable sealing does not test dynamic damping adjustment. Body and specs are absent, so allowable seal gaps and deformation limits are missing.

comparisons.objective: Place and orient two weld-neck flanges on riser stubs to plant centerlines, versus tune and lock a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Heavy circular-part placement, bore/stub alignment, and two-hole rotational orientation versus recessed-tool insertion, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and response-guided locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Both flanges seated and two-holed to specified centerlines versus two safe repeatable impacts within quantified limits.
comparisons.reason: Precision flange fit-up is distinct from adjustable energy-absorber commissioning. No specs provide angular, positional, or seating tolerances.

comparisons.objective: Place markers for a grid square and six-figure map reference, versus commission a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Map-convention reasoning and planar point placement versus contact-rich tool alignment, fine rotation, torque control, and physical cycle evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Markers at the correctly interpreted square and point versus two non-bottoming, non-overloaded stops with low rebound and retained setting.
comparisons.reason: Semantic map referencing and placement do not test mechanical adjustment or dynamic response. No specs add numeric placement tolerances.

comparisons.objective: Assemble and transfer a glass-plate casting cassette; candidate commissions and locks an adjustable axis damper through repeated impact trials.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cassette alignment, cam closure, spring-lever holding, and bimanual transfer versus recessed hex-key engagement, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Cassette must remain assembled and stable after placement; candidate requires two safe 0.85 J-or-greater cycles, ≤12 mm travel, no hard-stop strike/rebound/overload, and bounded post-lock drift. Cassette tolerances and damage gates are not stated.
comparisons.reason: Meaningfully different assembly/transfer ability; shared bimanual stabilization does not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Use a mirror to read an occluded fault code and fetch the named spare; candidate physically tunes and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Mirror positioning, indirect visual interpretation, and spare retrieval versus tool insertion, collar adjustment, counterholding, and force-controlled tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Referenced record provides no explicit scoring thresholds beyond reading and fetching; candidate requires a prescribed unlock-adjust-test-relock sequence and two bounded dynamic stops.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is indirect inspection and semantic selection, not mechanical commissioning; sparse rubric details do not create a plausible duplicate.

comparisons.objective: Move a dinghy above the tide line; candidate commissions a compact robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large-object relocation is implied, while the candidate tests precision hex-key use, fine rotary adjustment, counterholding, and iterative response-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: No dinghy placement threshold, stability rule, or damage rubric is provided; candidate has explicit energy, velocity, travel, rebound, hard-stop, locking, and drift gates.
comparisons.reason: Clearly unrelated transport objective despite missing dinghy rubric details.

comparisons.objective: Search boxes once each, retrieve buttons, and reclose them; candidate tunes and locks an industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual box restraint, sliding-lid operation, search memory, and item retrieval versus recessed tool engagement, fine collar rotation, and bounded locking torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires each box opened at most once, sequential closure, correct retrieval, and final reset; candidate requires physical unlock/relock and two safe repeatable impact cycles. Numeric lid and placement tolerances are unstated.
comparisons.reason: Search-state management and sliding-container manipulation differ materially from dynamic mechanical adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Coat violin-bow hair by stroking it over restrained rosin; candidate adjusts a damper to achieve repeatable carriage stops.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual long-object handling, surface contact, repeated stroking, and rosin restraint versus key insertion, collar tuning, counterholding, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Bow hair must be visibly coated and returned without displacing the holder; candidate uses measured travel, impact, rebound, overload, and drift gates. Coating and force thresholds are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Both use bimanual stabilization, but the tested contact process and feedback outcome are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Insert a loaded sheet pan into a rack slot while preventing rack motion; candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: One-hand rack bracing plus guided planar slot insertion versus small-tool alignment, fine rotation, locking torque, and iterative dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Pan must occupy the second slot while rack translation stays within 40 mm and the end state holds 1 s; candidate requires two safe impacts with ≤12 mm travel and no drift or hard-stop contact.
comparisons.reason: Constrained insertion into a mobile rack is not damper adjustment; bracing is only a shared generic primitive.

comparisons.objective: Sweep ceramic fragments from under a bench into a pan; candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Two-ended squeegee grasping, coordinated sweeping under occlusion, and fragment collection versus precision key insertion, collar rotation, counterholding, and force-limited fastening.
comparisons.success_condition: All four pieces must reach the pan, the tool be released, and the scene remain still for 1 s with yaw/tilt gates; candidate instead measures impact response and lock retention. Exact yaw/tilt thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual tool use is shared only generically; debris sweeping tests a different contact and coordination ability.

comparisons.objective: Present all six product faces to a camera and repack it; candidate commissions an axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Regrasping and controlled object reorientation for visual inspection versus recessed tool use, fine adjustment, counterholding, and force-controlled locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Only six-face presentation and repacking are stated; coverage tolerances, camera dwell, repack pose, and damage gates are missing. Candidate has explicit sequential and dynamic thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Inspection-oriented reorientation is meaningfully different; the sparse board rubric does not suggest duplication.

comparisons.objective: Touch three board test pads in order with a tethered probe and return it; candidate adjusts and validates a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fine probe-tip placement, one-second dwell, cable management, and holder insertion versus hex-key seating, collar tuning, counterholding, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Pads 1–3 must be contacted in order for ≥1 s each without the lead striking components, then the probe returned; candidate requires two safe carriage cycles and verified lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Both demand precise tool alignment, but electrical probing and dynamic mechanical commissioning test different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Transfer support of a gravity-loaded cover and control its closure; candidate tunes a damper through iterative impacts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support handoff and continuous gravity-load control versus key insertion, retained-collar adjustment, counterholding, and bounded fastener torque.
comparisons.success_condition: Observable closing speed is constrained, but its numeric limit and final pose tolerance are absent; candidate requires two cycles meeting explicit stroke, impact, rebound, overload, and drift gates.
comparisons.reason: Controlled closure tests load transfer and motion regulation, not parameter adjustment and post-lock validation.

comparisons.objective: Unload two books from a supporting hand, place them flat, and park that hand; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual support transfer, object separation, and stable placement versus precision tool engagement, collar rotation, counterholding, and tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Both books must be preserved and placed flat, with no mandated sequence; candidate requires ordered unlock-adjust-cycle-relock operations and measured dynamic performance. Flatness and damage thresholds are unstated.
comparisons.reason: Support unloading and placement are materially different from mechanical tuning.

comparisons.objective: Route a wire around formboard pins along a marked path and insert its plug; candidate tunes a rigid shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable cable routing, pin-side selection, tension management, and connector insertion versus rigid tool alignment, rotary adjustment, and force-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Wire must pass every pin on the marked side and the plug be seated; candidate requires two safe impacts and witness-tested setting retention. Cable clearance and insertion-depth tolerances are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Deformable routing and terminal insertion test a different ability from rigid damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Use a rake to extract chips from undercut T-slots into a collection bay; candidate adjusts and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: End-entry tool insertion beneath ledges, channel traversal, and chip pulling versus recessed key engagement, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: Five chips must leave three channels and the rake return to its supports; candidate uses explicit dynamic-cycle and lock-drift criteria. Chip/bay containment and tool-pose tolerances are unstated.
comparisons.reason: Undercut cleaning is distinct constrained tool use, not dynamic parameter tuning.

comparisons.objective: Identify two 8 cm spacers by measurement and kit only those parts; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual/physical ruler comparison, discrimination among similar parts, and pick-and-place versus hex-key insertion, fine rotation, stabilization, and iterative impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly both 8 cm spacers and nothing else must enter the cup; candidate requires ordered mechanical operations and two bounded carriage stops. Measurement tolerance is not stated.
comparisons.reason: Metrology-driven part selection differs materially from mechanical adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Refuse unauthorized card use and call a supervisor; candidate performs isolated damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Policy-sensitive choice and physical supervisor-button actuation versus tool alignment, collar tuning, counterholding, locking, and guarded cycle actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Colleague card must remain untouched, the run must not start, and supervisor must be called; candidate instead requires de-energized adjustment followed by two safe cycles. Button travel/dwell thresholds are absent.
comparisons.reason: Shared button pressing is incidental; the record tests safe refusal and authorization handling.

comparisons.objective: Join two 2×2 blocks across four studs and verify retention by lifting; candidate adjusts and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stud alignment, press-fit insertion, force application, and lift verification versus recessed key engagement, controlled collar rotation, counterholding, and tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: All four studs must engage and retain the lower block during lift before release; candidate requires measured dynamic response and post-lock drift control. Fit-force and alignment tolerances are unstated.
comparisons.reason: Press-fit assembly and retention lifting are different from tunable damping and fastener locking.

comparisons.objective: Join two 2×2 blocks with exactly two adjacent studs engaged and verify the cantilevered joint; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Offset stud alignment, partial press-fit engagement, force control, and cantilevered lift verification versus tool insertion, fine rotary tuning, counterholding, and torque-limited locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly two adjacent studs must engage and retain the unsupported lower block; candidate instead requires two safe impact cycles and lock stability. Fit-force thresholds are missing.
comparisons.reason: Partial-overlap press-fit assembly tests a distinct geometric and retention skill.

comparisons.objective: Fill a chemical day tank to a mark and close the transfer valve; candidate tunes an industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Valve operation and feedback-based liquid-level control versus hex-key alignment, collar adjustment, counterholding, and torque-controlled fastening.
comparisons.success_condition: Valve must be opened, level brought to the mark, and valve closed without overflow; candidate requires isolated adjustment and two safe carriage stops. Level tolerance, flow rate, and spill threshold are unstated.
comparisons.reason: Both involve feedback and final shutoff/locking, but fluid transfer control is a meaningfully different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Beat an egg in a pan while stabilizing the pan and containing the contents; candidate adjusts a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual vessel restraint, whisk grasping, repeated mixing contact, and spill avoidance versus precision key use, collar tuning, counterholding, and tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: Yolk and white must mix, only the whisk may touch the egg, and the flat pan must retain all contents; candidate uses stroke, impact, rebound, overload, and drift thresholds. Mixing uniformity and flatness thresholds are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Repeated mixing and containment differ materially from mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Resolve another person's left/right perspective and place a cup on the correct coaster; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Perspective reasoning followed by upright pick-and-place versus tool insertion, fine collar manipulation, counterholding, and iterative dynamic adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Cup center must be within a 4.5 cm coaster radius, on the coaster 15 cm right of robot midline, and within about 25° of vertical; candidate has unrelated impact and lock-retention gates.
comparisons.reason: Spatial perspective selection and placement do not duplicate damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Carry bars to a shelf without overhang or crossing striped exclusion regions; candidate commissions a compact damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual long-object transport and shelf placement versus small-tool alignment, rotary tuning, stabilization, and force-limited fastening.
comparisons.success_condition: Bars must be placed on the grey shelf and kept off stripes; exact overhang, contact, stability, and damage tolerances are not supplied. Candidate has explicit energy, stroke, impact, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Large-object transport and placement are clearly different despite incomplete shelf rubric details.

comparisons.objective: Count six bolts and place exactly half in a cup; candidate adjusts and validates a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Counting, repeated small-part grasping, and cup placement versus recessed key insertion, collar rotation, counterholding, and response-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly three bolts must be inside the cup below the wall tops; candidate requires an ordered adjustment sequence and two safe dynamic cycles. No bolt damage or final-stability thresholds are stated.
comparisons.reason: Quantity reasoning and repeated part transfer test a different ability.

comparisons.objective: Verify a GFCI by pressing TEST and then RESET; candidate adjusts a damper and operates a guarded cycle control.
comparisons.physical_skill: Order-sensitive button localization and depression versus hex-key engagement, fine collar tuning, bimanual stabilization, tightening, and control actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: TEST must trip the outlet before RESET restores it; RESET-then-TEST fails. Candidate additionally requires physical unlock/relock and two thresholded carriage cycles. Press force, travel, and electrical-state timing are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Physical control actuation is a shared generic primitive; GFCI sequence verification does not test mechanical tuning.

comparisons.objective: Unfold three tripod legs and leave the tripod standing in a marked square; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual articulated-leg manipulation, repeated regrasping, stance formation, and stable placement versus precision key insertion, collar rotation, counterholding, and torque control.
comparisons.success_condition: All three passive legs must be unfolded, tripod released inside the square, and stability maintained for 5 s; candidate requires two safe impacts and lock retention. Leg-angle and square-boundary tolerances are not stated.
comparisons.reason: Articulated deployment and balance are materially different from shock-absorber adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Thread four food pieces onto a skewer held level, then return the assembly to the grill; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual skewer stabilization, hole-to-point alignment, sequential insertion, sliding, and regrasping versus recessed key seating, fine rotary adjustment, counterholding, and bounded tightening.
comparisons.success_condition: All four pieces must be threaded, the skewer kept level and laid back across the grill; candidate requires two measured safe stops and low post-lock drift. Level, insertion-depth, and damage thresholds are unspecified.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve alignment and bimanual stabilization, sequential through-hole insertion is a meaningfully different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Measure a triangle and enter its area; unlike commissioning a shock absorber from dynamic response.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ruler placement, visual measurement, and calculator pressing; no setscrew unlocking, collar adjustment, or impact tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Submit 50 cm² within 120 seconds. No spec versions or damper-response thresholds are provided.
comparisons.reason: Tests geometric measurement and numeric entry, not mechanical adjustment and validation.

comparisons.objective: Open binder rings, thread a divider, and reclose them; unlike tuning and locking a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual ring actuation and six-hole alignment/insertion. It lacks iterative dynamic-response adjustment and torque-limited relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Open rings, release the divider on all six rings, then close them. No numeric tolerances or spec versions are supplied.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual manipulation is generic; the tested insertion and latching ability is meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Hoist and land a suspended bucket on a scaffold deck; unlike damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rope hauling, suspended-load control, bail handling, and coordinated landing; no fine rotary setting or setscrew work.
comparisons.success_condition: Tiered score for safe hoisting, landing, release, and stillness, with hands not under the load. Exact thresholds and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests dynamic suspended-load handling rather than adjustment of an impact absorber.

comparisons.objective: Remove two transport keys before unloading a captive carrier; unlike adjusting and validating a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Key extraction and ordered carrier handling; no hex-key-driven fastener, fine collar rotation, or repeated impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Both keys must be removed before unloading; the body references numerical scoring but does not state it, and no spec versions are included.
comparisons.reason: The sequencing and extraction task does not test damper tuning or lock retention.

comparisons.objective: Sort a power bank and large shampoo into bags according to airline rules; unlike mechanical commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Object recognition, grasping, and bag placement; no alignment with a recessed fastener, fine adjustment, or force-controlled locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Power bank must be in the cabin bag and shampoo over 100 ml in the hold case. No manipulation tolerances or spec versions are supplied.
comparisons.reason: Tests semantic rule application and packing, not adjustment of machine dynamics.

comparisons.objective: Rotate two hurdles so their feet face the runners' approach; unlike shock-absorber tuning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large-object reorientation and placement on marks; no tool insertion, retained adjustment, or dynamic-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Each upright hurdle on its marks with feet toward the start scores 0.5. No numeric placement tolerance or spec versions are stated.
comparisons.reason: Tests orientation knowledge and gross placement rather than fine mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Install correct end and mid clamps at six solar-panel positions; unlike commissioning a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clamp selection, alignment, seating, and fastening. Any fastening primitive is generic; there is no adjustment from repeated impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Each correct clamp type seated level at its proper position scores one sixth. Tightening torque and geometric tolerances are missing; no spec versions exist.
comparisons.reason: Tests component selection and multi-position panel clamping, not variable damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Scrape a stuck print from a build plate and place it in a basket; unlike shock-absorber commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grasp a scraper, insert its thin blade under an edge, lever the print free, and transfer it; no rotary tuning or locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Print freed and placed in basket, plate left in printer, scraper returned to table. Force/damage thresholds and spec versions are not given.
comparisons.reason: Tests tool-mediated separation and transfer rather than setting and validating a damper.

comparisons.objective: Position a rain gauge clear of a wall and orient an instrument-screen door north; unlike damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Gross relocation and orientation using spatial constraints; no fine tool engagement, locking torque, or impact observation.
comparisons.success_condition: Gauge distance must be at least twice obstacle height and the door must face north. Angular/placement tolerances and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests site-layout knowledge and object orientation, not machine adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Measure a training doll by straightening its sprung legs and closing a footboard; unlike tuning a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual restraint of compliant legs while positioning a measuring board; no fastener manipulation or repeated cycle evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Leave the footboard at the length reading and release. The body omits numeric tolerances and scoring details; no spec versions are present.
comparisons.reason: Tests compliant-body positioning and measurement, a meaningfully different ability.

comparisons.objective: Land a container on twistlocks and lock them; unlike adjusting a compact damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Heavy-object alignment and landing followed by lock rotation; no recessed setscrew engagement, fine damping adjustment, or response-based iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Container must be landed and both twistlocks turned, followed by arm retreat. Alignment tolerances and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Although both include rotation and locking, container registration and twistlock closure test different mechanics.

comparisons.objective: Fit each quadcopter motor with a propeller matching its rotation direction; unlike damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select handed propellers and align/install them on motor shafts; no iterative dynamic-response tuning or retained collar adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Leading edges must lead in each motor's direction. The body supplies no scoring rubric, tolerances, or spec versions.
comparisons.reason: Tests handed-part selection and assembly rather than damping calibration.

comparisons.objective: Start a clock, collect five pens into a holder, and stop the clock; unlike damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Button pressing and repeated small-object pick-and-place; no tool-fastener engagement, fine rotary tuning, or lock verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Required start/collection/stop order, physical containment/support, and release; exact tolerances are absent and there are no spec versions.
comparisons.reason: Tests timed sequencing and multi-object collection, not mechanical response adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Join two lower robot-leg links by clicking a stud into a jaw; unlike commissioning a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bring articulated links into alignment and perform snap-fit insertion; no setscrew unlocking, fine collar rotation, or cycle-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Orange stud must click into blue jaw and the robot must release. Engagement-force/tolerance details and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests constrained link alignment and snap latching rather than adjustable damping.

comparisons.objective: Flip a pancake in a pan with a turner; unlike shock-absorber commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual pan stabilization, blade insertion under a compliant object, and controlled flipping; no fastener or adjustment mechanism.
comparisons.success_condition: Pancake inverted in pan, turner returned, pan released, and arms retracted. Spill/damage thresholds and spec versions are not stated.
comparisons.reason: Shared stabilization is generic; the core utensil insertion and flipping ability is unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Select one requested M4×20 screw and place it alone in a handoff tray; unlike adjusting a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-part identification, bin picking, transfer, and release; the screw is handled as an object rather than driven as a fastener.
comparisons.success_condition: One correct screw alone in tray, wrong sizes unmoved, and nothing grasped. Placement tolerances and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests part selection and handoff, not hex-key engagement or mechanical tuning.

comparisons.objective: Select one requested M4×20 screw and place it alone in a handoff tray; unlike adjusting a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-part identification, bin picking, transfer, and release; no screw driving, collar rotation, or dynamic evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: One correct screw alone in tray, wrong sizes unmoved, and grippers released. Placement tolerances and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Despite duplicating pr-1445, it remains distinct from the candidate's commissioning task.

comparisons.objective: Hide, track, and retrieve a ball through a cup shuffle; unlike damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual cup lifting, ball placement/retrieval, and visual memory across motion; no fastener manipulation or force calibration.
comparisons.success_condition: Follow the hide/start/wait/retrieve/reset sequence, with the first lifted cup correct. Exact pose tolerances and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests object permanence, tracking, and ordered bimanual handling rather than machine adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Move an aircraft flap lever through a gated quadrant into FULL; unlike tuning and locking a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained lever manipulation through a gate and into a detent. Fine motion is shared generically, but there is no tool use or iterative response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Lever must reach the FULL detent by the red stop and be released. Path/detent tolerances and spec versions are not given.
comparisons.reason: Tests following a gated kinematic path and detent seating, not calibrated damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Install an arch keystone before removing wooden centering; unlike shock-absorber commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and insert a wedge-shaped load-bearing stone, then remove temporary support; no fine fastener engagement or dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Arch must remain standing after centering removal, implying correct keystone installation. Numeric stability/tolerance details and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests structural sequencing and load-bearing insertion rather than impact-response calibration.

comparisons.objective: Roll a fallen robot dog off its legs, remove its battery, and place it on a charger; unlike damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Whole-body reorientation, stabilization, battery extraction, and transfer; no rotary adjustment or setscrew retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Battery must be removed and placed on the charging pad. The body lacks detailed scoring, safety thresholds, and spec versions.
comparisons.reason: Tests access creation and component removal from an unstable assembly, not tuning.

comparisons.objective: Replace a frayed USB cable in the same hub port; unlike shock-absorber commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hub counterholding, straight connector extraction, same-port alignment, and full insertion. Shared stabilization/insertion primitives are generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Old plug removed and binned before new plug leaves dock; new plug fully inserted only into the original port; arms return. Force/tolerance details and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests connector replacement and strict sequencing, not fine rotary adjustment or repeated impact validation.

comparisons.objective: Unlock and move two paper-cassette guides snug against a stack; unlike tuning and locking a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Squeeze release tabs while sliding guides, then release to latch. This superficially shares unlock-adjust-lock, but uses linear guide positioning against paper rather than tool-driven rotary calibration from dynamics.
comparisons.success_condition: Both guides snug against the stack without moving it and released in the locked state. Snugness tolerance, paper-motion threshold, and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: The mechanism and tested feedback differ meaningfully: direct geometric contact versus iterative impact-response tuning and witness-torque retention.

comparisons.objective: Vent a pressure pan before removing and placing its lid; unlike damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a vent control, wait for steam to stop, lift a lid level by its knob, and place it on a trivet; no fastener or tuning operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Vent first, remove lid only after steam stops, place it flat, release, and withdraw. Exact pressure/steam/timing thresholds and spec versions are absent.
comparisons.reason: Tests safety-critical ordered actuation and lid handling rather than adjustable damping.

comparisons.objective: Vent a pressure pan before removing and placing its lid; unlike damper commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Button holding and level lid transfer after a physical wait condition; no recessed tool engagement, collar adjustment, or lock test.
comparisons.success_condition: Vent must precede lid removal; lid ends flat on trivet with grippers released and withdrawn. Numeric thresholds and spec versions are absent.
